questions.question: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 124(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President of India** is the constitutional authority empowered to appoint the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** and every other **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• The appointment follows the **seniority principle**, where the **outgoing Chief Justice** recommends the name of the **senior-most judge** of the Supreme Court to the **Union Ministry of Law and Justice**.
 
• While the **Union Law Minister** forwards the recommendation to the **Prime Minister**, who then advises the **President**, the **President** remains the ultimate appointing authority under their **seal and warrant**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** has established through the **Second Judges Case (1993)** and **Third Judges Case (1998)** that the **President** must act in accordance with the recommendations of the **Collegium**, which consists of the **CJI** and the **four senior-most judges**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court of India**:

 
 
• Established under **Part V**, **Chapter IV** (Articles 124 to 147) of the **Constitution**, it serves as the **apex judicial body**.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** holds office until the age of **65 years**.
 
• The **CJI** administers the oath of office to the **President**, and conversely, the **President** administers the oath to the **CJI**.
 
 
 
• **Removal Procedure**:
 
 
• A **Judge** can only be removed by the **President** following an address by **Parliament** supported by a **special majority** in both houses.
 
• The grounds for removal are limited to **proved misbehaviour** or **incapacity** as per the **Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968**.

questions.question: The Council of Ministers at the Union level is responsible to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 75(3)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Union Council of Ministers** is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People).
 
• The principle of **Collective Responsibility** implies that the entire **Ministry** is at the helm of affairs only as long as it enjoys the confidence of the **majority** in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• If a **No-Confidence Motion** is passed in the **Lok Sabha**, the entire **Council of Ministers**, including those ministers who are members of the **Rajya Sabha**, must resign immediately.
 
• This accountability ensures that the **Executive** remains subservient to the **Legislature**, which represents the direct will of the citizens in a **Parliamentary Democracy**.
 
• The **Council of Ministers** functions as a single unit; therefore, a vote of no confidence against a single minister is effectively a vote against the entire **Cabinet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• While the **Council of Ministers** is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**, individual ministers hold office during the **pleasure of the President** under **Article 75(2)**. This is known as **Individual Responsibility**.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha**:
 
 
• Although ministers can be chosen from the **Rajya Sabha**, the council is not responsible to this **Upper House**. The **Rajya Sabha** can discuss policies but cannot remove the government through a **No-Confidence Motion**.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court**:
 
 
• The **Judiciary** performs **Judicial Review** to check the constitutionality of executive actions but does not hold the **Council of Ministers** politically accountable for day-to-day administration.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Lodi dynasty, the last ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahlul Lodi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lodi dynasty** was the fifth and final ruling family of the **Delhi Sultanate**, governing from **1451 to 1526 AD**.
 
• **Bahlul Lodi** (reigned **1451−1489**) founded the dynasty after the abdication of the last **Sayyid ruler**, **Alam Shah**.
 
• He belonged to the **Shahu Khel** clan of the **Pashtun** (Afghan) **Lodi** tribe, making this the first **Afghan dynasty** to rule over Delhi.
 
• During his 38-year reign, he successfully suppressed various rebellions and annexed the **Sharqi dynasty** of **Jaunpur** in **1479**, which significantly expanded his territory.
 
• He is historically noted for his **tribal democratic** approach, where he treated his **Afghan nobles** as peers rather than subordinates, often sitting on the floor with them to ensure their loyalty and cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikandar Lodi** (**1489−1517**):

 
 
• He was the son of Bahlul Lodi and is regarded as the most powerful ruler of the dynasty.
 
• He founded the city of **Agra** in **1504** and shifted the capital from Delhi to Agra.
 
• He introduced the **Gazz-i-Sikandari**, a standardized unit for land measurement consisting of **32 digits**.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi** (**1517−1526**):
 
 
• He was the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty and the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• His autocratic style and insistence on royal supremacy led to conflict with his Afghan nobles, prompting **Daulat Khan Lodi** to invite **Babur** to invade India.
 
• He was defeated and killed in the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**, which ended the Sultanate era and established the **Mughal Empire**.

questions.question: The Simon Commission (1927) faced boycott because
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It excluded Indian members.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Simon Commission**, officially known as the **Indian Statutory Commission**, was sent to India in **1928** (constituted in **November 1927**) to review the functioning of the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• The commission was headed by **Sir John Simon** and consisted of **seven members** drawn from the British Parliament.
 
• The fundamental reason for the nationwide boycott was that the commission was an **all-white** body, entirely **excluding Indian members**, which was seen as a denial of the right of Indians to participate in deciding their own constitutional future.
 
• Political groups across the spectrum, including the **Indian National Congress** (during the **1927 Madras Session**) and the **All India Muslim League**, resolved to boycott the commission.
 
• Protests were characterized by the slogan **Go Back Simon** and black flag demonstrations upon the commission's arrival in cities like **Bombay** and **Lahore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Demands and Proposals:**

 
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** While the Simon Commission actually recommended the abolition of **dyarchy** and the implementation of **Provincial Autonomy** in its **1930 report**, this was not the cause of the initial boycott.
 
• **Dominion Status:** The commission notably refrained from mentioning **Dominion Status** as a goal for India, which further aggravated Indian leaders who sought it as a minimum requirement.
 
• **Separate Electorates:** The commission recommended the continuation of **Separate Electorates** for communal representation, a system that remained a point of contention between different political factions.
 
• **Impact on National Movement:** The protests led to the tragic death of **Lala Lajpat Rai** following a **lathi charge** in **Lahore**, which radicalized the Indian youth and accelerated the demand for **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
 
• **Nehru Report:** In response to the challenge by **Lord Birkenhead** (Secretary of State) that Indians could not draft a constitution, the **Nehru Report (1928)** was prepared by an all-party committee.

questions.question: What is another name for a market economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capitalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Market Economy** is an economic system where the production and pricing of goods and services are determined by the **interactions** of a country's individual citizens and businesses.
 
• The term **Capitalism** is used interchangeably with a market economy because it is based on the **private ownership** of the **means of production** and the creation of goods for **profit**.
 
• In this system, the **allocation of resources** is handled by the **price mechanism**, which is driven by the **law of supply and demand** rather than by a **central planning authority**.
 
• Fundamental features of this economy include **capital accumulation**, **competitive markets**, **voluntary exchange**, and a **decentralized** decision-making process.
 
• Economists like **Adam Smith** argued that the **invisible hand** of the market would lead to the most efficient economic outcomes without the need for **government intervention**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socialism**:

 
 
• Refers to an economic system where the **means of production** are owned or regulated by the **state** or **community**.
 
• Focuses on **social equity** and the distribution of resources based on **social need** rather than individual **profit**.
 
 
 
• **Communism**:
 
 
• A radical form of socialism that advocates for a **classless society** where all property is **publicly owned**.
 
• It seeks to eliminate the **private sector** entirely, which is the cornerstone of a **market economy**.
 
 
 
• **Feudalism**:
 
 
• A historical social and economic system used in **medieval Europe** based on **land ownership** and **military service**.
 
• Unlike modern economies, it relied on a **rigid hierarchy** of **lords** and **serfs** rather than **free-market exchange**.

questions.question: In aerobic breakdown of pyruvate (in mitochondria), which of the following is formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide + water + energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerobic respiration** is a high-efficiency metabolic process that utilizes **Oxygen** to break down organic molecules for cellular energy.
 
• The process initiates in the **Cytoplasm** through **Glycolysis**, where a single **Glucose** molecule is converted into two **Pyruvate** molecules.
 
• In the presence of oxygen, **Pyruvate** is transported into the **Mitochondria**, where it undergoes oxidative decarboxylation to become **Acetyl-CoA** before entering the **Krebs Cycle**.
 
• Within the **Mitochondrial Matrix** and the **Inner Mitochondrial Membrane**, the carbon atoms in pyruvate are completely oxidized to form **Carbon dioxide** (CO₂).
 
• The **Electron Transport Chain** (ETC) facilitates the transfer of electrons to oxygen, the final electron acceptor, resulting in the formation of **Water** (H₂O).
 
• This mitochondrial breakdown is the primary source of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), yielding approximately **30 to 32 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, which constitutes the **Energy** used for cellular functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaerobic Respiration Pathways**:

 
 
• **Lactic Acid Formation**: This occurs in **Muscle Cells** during vigorous exercise when oxygen levels are depleted. Pyruvate is converted into **Lactic Acid** and energy, which can lead to muscle fatigue.
 
• **Ethanol Fermentation**: Typically observed in **Yeast** and certain bacteria, this anaerobic process converts pyruvate into **Ethanol**, **Carbon dioxide**, and energy. This is a fundamental process in the **Brewing** and **Baking** industries.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Known as the **Powerhouse of the Cell**, these organelles possess their own **Mitochondrial DNA** and a double-membrane structure.
 
• The inner membrane is folded into **Cristae** to increase the surface area for the enzymes involved in the **ATP synthase** process.

questions.question: The Swachhata Hi Seva campaign 2024, observed the theme ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swabhav Swachhata, Sanskaar Swachhata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2024** campaign was observed from **September 17** (Sewa Diwas) to **October 2, 2024** (Swachh Bharat Diwas).
 
• The theme for the 2024 edition was **Swabhav Swachhata, Sanskaar Swachhata**, which translates to **'Cleanliness of Nature, Cleanliness of Culture'**.
 
• This year marks the **10th anniversary** of the launch of the **Swachh Bharat Mission** (SBM) in 2014.
 
• The campaign is a joint initiative led by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** and the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
 
• It focuses on massive advocacy and community mobilization to strengthen the commitment toward a **cleaner India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2024 campaign was structured around **three primary pillars**:

 
 
• **Swachhata Ki Bhagidari**: Encouraging public participation through large-scale **awareness activities** and community engagement.
 
• **Sampoorna Swachhata**: Focusing on the transformation of **Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs)**, which involve clearing difficult and neglected waste spots across the country.
 
• **Safai Mitra Suraksha Shivirs**: Organizing camps to provide **health check-ups**, safety equipment, and social security benefits to sanitation workers.
 
 
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Mission** was launched on **October 2, 2014**, with the vision of achieving an **Open Defecation Free (ODF)** nation.
 
• **SBM-Urban 2.0** and **SBM-Gramin Phase II** are currently being implemented to ensure **sustainable sanitation** and **100 percent scientific processing** of solid waste.
 
• Previous themes included **'Garbage Free India'** for the year **2023**, highlighting the evolution of the campaign's focus areas.

questions.question: Which city served as the capital of the Pandya Kings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madurai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pandya Dynasty** was one of the three major **Tamil kingdoms** of Southern India, collectively known as the **Muventar**, alongside the Cholas and the Cheras.
 
• **Madurai**, located on the banks of the **Vaigai River**, served as the primary and most enduring capital of the **Pandyas** from ancient times through the medieval period.
 
• The city was the epicenter of **Tamil culture** and the seat of the **Sangam assemblies**, where scholarly poets gathered under royal patronage to compile the **Sangam literature**.
 
• The **Pandyas** initially controlled the southern tip of the Indian peninsula, and their early capital and major port was **Korkai**, famous for its **pearl fishery**, before the administrative center shifted inland to **Madurai**.
 
• The dynasty adopted the **Fish** as its royal emblem, symbolizing their dominance over the coastal regions and the **Indian Ocean** trade routes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ujjain**:

 
 
• Located in the **Malwa** region of **Madhya Pradesh**, it was the ancient capital of the **Avanti** Mahajanapada.
 
• It served as a vital trade hub connecting North and West India and was a center for **Hindu astronomy**.
 
 
 
• **Vaishali**:
 
 
• Situated in modern-day **Bihar**, it was the capital of the **Vrijji confederacy** and the **Licchavi** clan.
 
• It is celebrated as the site of one of the world's first **republican** governments (Gana-Sangha).
 
 
 
• **Amravati**:
 
 
• Located in the **Guntur** district of **Andhra Pradesh**, it served as the capital for the **Satavahana Dynasty** under the name **Dhanyakataka**.
 
• It is architecturally significant for the **Great Stupa**, a masterpiece of **Buddhist art** and the **Amaravati school** of sculpture.

questions.question:
Which of the following is part of the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution?

I. Forests

II. Banking
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forests** were originally part of the **State List** but were moved to the **Concurrent List** (List III) of the **Seventh Schedule** following the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976**. This allows both the **Union Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to enact laws concerning forest conservation and management. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Banking** is a subject of national importance that requires a uniform policy throughout the country. It is explicitly listed under **Entry 45** of the **Union List** (List I) in the **Seventh Schedule**. Therefore, only the **Central Government** has the exclusive power to make laws related to banking operations and the **Reserve Bank of India**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule**: Under **Article 246**, the Constitution classifies legislative powers into three lists to maintain the federal structure of **India**.

 
 
• **Union List (List I)**: Includes subjects like **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Railways**, and **Atomic Energy**. It currently contains 100 subjects.
 
• **State List (List II)**: Includes subjects like **Police**, **Public Health**, **Agriculture**, and **Local Government**. It currently contains 61 subjects.
 
• **Concurrent List (List III)**: Includes subjects like **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, and **Trade Unions**. It currently contains 52 subjects.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**: This landmark amendment transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**, namely:
 
 
• **Education**
 
• **Forests**
 
• **Weights and Measures**
 
• **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**
 
• **Administration of Justice**
 
 
 
• **Residuary Powers**: Subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists fall under **Residuary Powers**, which are vested in the **Union Parliament** as per **Article 248**.

questions.question: Which festival of Mizoram is celebrated as a thanksgiving after clearing the forests for jhum cultivation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chapchar Kut**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chapchar Kut** is the most significant and oldest traditional festival celebrated by the people of **Mizoram**, often referred to as the **Festival of Spring**.
 
• It is observed as a **thanksgiving** ceremony following the arduous task of **clearing forests** (cutting and burning trees) for **Jhum cultivation**, which is the traditional slash-and-burn agricultural practice of the region.
 
• The festival is typically celebrated in the month of **March**, marking the interval between the burning of the forest debris and the arrival of the first rains for sowing seeds.
 
• A major highlight of the festivities is the performance of the **Cheraw** dance, also known as the **Bamboo Dance**, where performers display intricate footwork between rhythmically tapped bamboo poles.
 
• It represents a period of communal joy and peace, where the **Mizo** people dress in vibrant traditional attire, participate in grand feasts, and sing folk songs to celebrate their cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dree**:

 
 
• This is an agricultural festival celebrated by the **Apatani** tribe in **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• It is observed to seek the blessings of deities for a successful harvest and to protect crops from insects and famine.
 
 
 
• **Losar**:
 
 
• It marks the **Tibetan New Year** and is celebrated with great fervor in **Arunachal Pradesh** (by the Monpa tribe), **Sikkim**, and **Ladakh**.
 
• The festival involves cleaning homes, religious offerings, and masked dances in Buddhist monasteries.
 
 
 
• **Beh-dien-khlam**:
 
 
• This is a major socio-religious festival of the **Pnar** (Jaintia) people in **Meghalaya**.
 
• The literal meaning is **Chasing away the Plague**, performed to drive away evil spirits and ensure the well-being of the community.

questions.question: The National Rainfed Area Authority operates under which of the following Ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA)** was constituted by the Government of India on **November 3, 2006**, as an expert body to provide technical inputs for the planning and management of **rainfed farming**.
 
• It functions as an attached office under the **Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** within the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.
 
• The mandate of the NRAA is to address the ecological, social, and economic problems of **rainfed areas**, which account for nearly **51 percent** of the net sown area and support **40 percent** of the human and **60 percent** of the livestock population in India.
 
• The authority provides technical assistance for the **convergence** of various schemes like the **Watershed Development Component** of **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**.
 
• It is headed by a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)** and operates under the guidance of a **Governing Board** chaired by the **Union Agriculture Minister**.
 
• NRAA plays a crucial role in improving the **agricultural productivity** and **sustainability** of fragile ecosystems through holistic development strategies and climate-resilient farming practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti**:

 
 
• Formed in **May 2019** by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
 
• Responsible for the **Jal Jeevan Mission**, **Namami Gange**, and national river interlinking projects.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Cooperation**:
 
 
• Established in **July 2021** to realize the vision of **Sahakar se Samriddhi** (Prosperity through Cooperation).
 
• Focuses on strengthening the **cooperative movement** and streamlining the processes for **Multi-State Cooperative Societies**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Earth Sciences**:
 
 
• Formed in **2006**, it deals with **oceanography**, **meteorology**, and seismology.
 
• Oversees institutes like the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the **National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)**.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a hearing aid?

options.text: To convert sound waves into light signals
To amplify sound for clearer hearing
To change the frequency of sound

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To amplify sound for clearer hearing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary function of a **hearing aid** is **amplification**, which involves increasing the **intensity** or **amplitude** of sound waves to make them audible for individuals with hearing impairments.
 
• Scientifically, the device acts as an **electroacoustic transducer**. It uses a **microphone** to capture sound waves and convert them into **electrical signals**, which are then processed and strengthened.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, Rajasthan the biggest state in terms of area, has only _____ of the total population of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011**, the total population of **Rajasthan** was recorded at approximately **6.85 crore** (68,548,437), which constitutes about **5.66%** of **India’s total population** of **121.05 crore**.
 
• Among the given options, **5.5%** is the nearest and most accepted figure in various state-level examinations representing Rajasthan's share of the national population.
 
• Rajasthan is the **largest state** in India by geographical area, covering **3,42,239 square kilometers**, which is about **10.41%** of the total land area of the country.
 
• Despite its vast landmass, the state’s population share is relatively lower due to the presence of the **Thar Desert** and arid climatic conditions, which restrict high-density settlements in western regions.
 
• In terms of population ranking during the **2011 Census**, Rajasthan was the **seventh most populous** state in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan Demographic Indicators (Census 2011)**:

 
 
• **Population Density**: The state has a density of **200 persons per square kilometer**, which is much lower than the national average of **382**.
 
• **Sex Ratio**: The sex ratio in Rajasthan stands at **928 females** per 1000 males.
 
• **Literacy Rate**: The overall literacy rate of the state is **66.11%**, with male literacy at **79.19%** and female literacy at **52.12%**.
 
• **Decadal Growth**: The population growth rate between 2001 and 2011 was **21.31%**.
 
• **District Data**: **Jaipur** is the most populated district, while **Jaisalmer** is the least populated district in the state.

questions.question: In the context of money supply in India, ____ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government of India in the open market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Open market operation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** are the primary tools used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to regulate the **money supply** and maintain **liquidity** within the Indian economy.
 
• This process involves the purchase and sale of **Government Securities (G-Secs)**, such as **Treasury Bills** and **dated securities**, directly in the open market to or from commercial banks and financial institutions.
 
• When the **RBI** determines that there is excess liquidity (which may lead to high **inflation**), it **sells government bonds**. This action mops up cash from the banking system, thereby reducing the funds available for lending.
 
• Conversely, to boost liquidity and stimulate economic activity, the **RBI purchases bonds** from the market, injecting fresh capital into the banking system and lowering the cost of credit.
 
• **OMOs** serve as a **quantitative instrument** of **monetary policy**, helping the central bank influence **short-term interest rates** and align them with the **Policy Repo Rate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moral Suasion**:

 
 
• This is a **qualitative** or **selective credit control** method where the **RBI** uses psychological pressure and persuasion through meetings and circulars to convince banks to comply with its **monetary guidelines**.
 
 
 
• **Margin Requirement**:
 
 
• This refers to the difference between the **market value of security** (collateral) offered for a loan and the actual amount of **credit** granted. It is used to restrict the flow of credit to speculative or unproductive sectors.
 
 
 
• **Evergreening of loans**:
 
 
• It is a banking practice where a lender provides a **new loan** to a borrower to repay an **existing debt**. This is often done to prevent the original loan from being classified as a **Non-Performing Asset (NPA)**.

questions.question: In which Olympics did Michael Phelps won his record 8 gold Olympic medals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Michael Phelps** achieved the historic feat of winning **eight gold medals** in a single Olympic Games during the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• This performance broke the long-standing record held by **Mark Spitz**, who won **seven gold medals** at the **1972 Munich Olympics**.
 
• Phelps won gold in the **400m Individual Medley**, **200m Freestyle**, **100m Butterfly**, **200m Butterfly**, **200m Individual Medley**, **4×100m Freestyle Relay**, **4×200m Freestyle Relay**, and **4×100m Medley Relay**.
 
• In addition to winning gold in every event he entered, Phelps set **seven world records** and one **Olympic record** (in the 100m butterfly) during the competition.
 
• The **Water Cube** (Beijing National Aquatics Center) was the venue where Phelps completed this unprecedented achievement on **August 17, 2008**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2004 Athens Olympics**:

 
 
• Phelps won **six gold** and **two bronze medals** at the age of 19.
 
• He became the second male swimmer to win more than six medals in one Olympic Games.
 
 
 
• **2012 London Olympics**:
 
 
• He secured **four gold** and **two silver medals**.
 
• During these games, he surpassed Soviet gymnast **Larisa Latynina** to become the most decorated Olympian of all time.
 
 
 
• **2016 Rio Olympics**:
 
 
• In his final Olympic appearance, Phelps won **five gold** and **one silver medal**.
 
• He retired with a total of **28 Olympic medals**, including **23 gold**, **3 silver**, and **2 bronze**, across five Olympic appearances (2000−2016).

questions.question: The Philadelphi Corridor recently is located along the border of Gaza and ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Egypt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Philadelphi Corridor**, which is also referred to as the **Saladin Axis**, is a narrow strip of land approximately **14 kilometers** (8.7 miles) long and about 100 meters wide.
 
• It is geographically situated along the entire border between the **Gaza Strip** and the country of **Egypt**, stretching from the **Mediterranean Sea** to the **Kerem Shalom** border crossing.
 
• This buffer zone was established under the terms of the **1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty** to serve as a demilitarized area between the two nations.
 
• The primary strategic objective of the corridor is to act as a **security barrier** to prevent the smuggling of illicit materials, weapons, and personnel between the **Sinai Peninsula** and Gaza.
 
• The **Rafah Crossing**, which is the only land exit from the Gaza Strip not directly bordering Israel, is located along this critical corridor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Philadelphi Accord (2005)**:

 
 
• Following Israel's **unilateral disengagement** from Gaza in 2005, Israel and Egypt signed this specific accord to regulate the security of the border.
 
• It authorized Egypt to deploy **750 border guards** equipped with light weaponry to patrol the area and combat **terrorism** and **cross-border smuggling**.
 
• The accord ensured that the Egyptian deployment was for security purposes rather than military aggression, maintaining the spirit of the **Camp David Accords**.
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments**:
 
 
• The corridor has gained significant international attention during the **2023-2024 Israel-Hamas conflict**, as control over this strip is viewed as vital for neutralizing underground **smuggling tunnels**.
 
• Geopolitically, the corridor remains one of the most sensitive zones in the **Middle East**, directly impacting the humanitarian and security situation in the region.

questions.question: Who among the following never won an Olympic medal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sania Mirza**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PV Sindhu** is a decorated **badminton** player who secured a **Silver medal** at the **2016 Rio Olympics** and a **Bronze medal** at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sania Mirza**, a former **World No. 1** in doubles, participated in four **Olympic Games** (2008, 2012, 2016, 2020) but never won a medal, finishing fourth in the **Mixed Doubles** at **Rio 2016**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Saina Nehwal** made history by winning the **Bronze medal** in **Badminton** at the **2012 London Olympics**, becoming the first Indian shuttler to win an Olympic medal. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mary Kom**, an iconic boxer, clinched the **Bronze medal** in the **flyweight category** during the **2012 London Olympics**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sania Mirza**:

 
 
• She has won six **Grand Slam** titles, including three in **Women's Doubles** and three in **Mixed Doubles**.
 
• She was awarded the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in 2015 and the **Padma Bhushan** in 2016 for her contributions to sports.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Milestones for India**:
 
 
• **Karnam Malleswari** was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (Bronze in **Weightlifting**, 2000).
 
• **PV Sindhu** is the only Indian woman to win two individual **Olympic medals**.
 
• **Leander Paes** remains the only Indian to win an **Olympic medal** in **Tennis** (Bronze, 1996).
